::: {#rem-entropy-chain-rule-from-surprisal}
#### The chain rule for entropy is the chain rule for surprisal on average

@thm-surprisal-chain-rule holds for each pair of [values](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-realization) $(x, y)$ with positive [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability).
Each [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) in @thm-entropy-chain-rule
is the [expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) of the matching [surprisal](#def-surprisal),
by @def-joint-entropy, @rem-entropy-expected-surprisal and @def-conditional-entropy:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\entropyf{X, Y} &= \E{\surprisalf{X, Y}} \\
\entropyf{X} &= \E{\surprisalf{X}} \\
\entropyf{Y \mid X} &= \E{\surprisalf{Y \mid X}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

So the chain rule for entropy is the chain rule for surprisal,
averaged over the pair $(X, Y)$.
The [joint surprisal](#def-joint-surprisal) is the surprisal of the pair $(X, Y)$,
so the [joint entropy](#def-joint-entropy) is also the entropy of that pair.

:::
